description: We are young innovators passionate about climate science, Earth observation and technology. Our interests and skills include software development, GIS, environmental research and data visualisation. Through ClimateLens Uganda, we aim to make climate trends easier for communities to explore and understand. We welcome participants skilled in remote sensing, climate data analysis, programming, UI/UX design and environmental communication.
summary:
ClimateLens Uganda is an interactive climate information platform designed to help people explore and understand historical climate trends across Uganda using NASA Earth observation data.

The project focuses on making rainfall and temperature information more accessible through geographical visualisation and clear, understandable explanations. By exploring different locations, users can investigate how environmental conditions vary across Uganda and how climate patterns have changed over time.

Climate information is often available through technical datasets that are difficult for ordinary people to interpret. ClimateLens Uganda addresses this challenge by bringing climate observations into a more accessible digital experience.

The platform is intended for students, farmers, researchers, educators and local decision-makers interested in understanding climate variability.

By connecting NASA environmental information with interactive geographical exploration, ClimateLens Uganda aims to strengthen climate awareness, encourage scientific learning and support more informed discussions about environmental change.
details:
ClimateLens Uganda

Exploring Uganda's Climate Through NASA Earth Observation Data

The Problem

Climate variability affects agriculture, water resources, infrastructure and livelihoods across Uganda. Changes in rainfall and temperature can influence farming seasons, water availability and environmental conditions.

Although NASA provides extensive environmental datasets, much of this information is difficult for people without specialised scientific training to interpret.

ClimateLens Uganda was developed to make climate information easier to explore and understand.

Our Solution

ClimateLens Uganda is an interactive web-based platform focused on exploring historical climate conditions across Uganda.

The project aims to transform environmental observations into accessible geographical visualisations that help users understand rainfall patterns, temperature variations and longer-term climate trends.

Rather than requiring users to work directly with complicated scientific datasets, ClimateLens Uganda provides a more approachable way to investigate environmental information.

How the Platform Works

1. Geographical Exploration

Users explore Uganda and examine climate information associated with different locations.

2. Historical Climate Information

The platform focuses on rainfall and temperature observations, helping users explore environmental conditions over time.

3. Climate Visualisation

Climate information is communicated through geographical displays and understandable visualisations.

4. Regional Comparisons

The project is designed to help users recognise differences in environmental conditions between locations.

5. Climate Education

The platform supports learning by connecting scientific observations with environmental conditions relevant to Uganda.

NASA Earth Observation Data

NASA environmental resources provide the scientific foundation for the project.

Historical precipitation and temperature datasets are particularly relevant because they help users examine environmental variability across different periods and locations.

NASA POWER is a suitable source for these indicators where integrated into the application.

Innovation

ClimateLens Uganda focuses on the accessibility and geographical relevance of climate information.

Its approach combines Earth observation, geographical exploration and climate communication in a platform centred on Uganda.

The project aims to help users move beyond raw scientific numbers and better understand how environmental conditions differ across locations and time.

Intended Beneficiaries

Farmers: Explore historical rainfall and temperature patterns relevant to agricultural planning.

Students and Educators: Learn about climate variability through interactive geographical information.

Researchers: Explore environmental observations and regional climate patterns.

Local Decision-Makers: Access understandable climate information that can support environmental awareness and planning discussions.

Scientific Considerations

Historical climate observations describe past environmental conditions and do not guarantee future rainfall or temperature.

Climate trends also depend on the time period, geographical coverage and scientific methods used in the analysis.

The platform is intended for climate exploration and education rather than precise weather forecasting.

Future Development

Potential improvements include additional NASA environmental datasets, expanded historical comparisons, more detailed geographical analysis and improved accessibility for users with different technical backgrounds.

Conclusion

ClimateLens Uganda aims to make NASA Earth observation information more accessible to people across Uganda.

By bringing environmental observations into an interactive geographical experience, the project supports climate education, environmental awareness and better understanding of changing climate conditions.
